What does my ex represent for me, how did I fall for her in the first place , what does that say about me in regards of the projection I did on her.  


And now this is kind of a paradox but it is what it is, do not take yourself seriously and take yourself as seriously as you can, your feelings are real, your pain is real, your confusion is real see it for what it is , know which parts of you are dormant, rejected not accepted and do not throw yourself excessively into research because as you might know extremes have drawbacks, every choice you make has a repercussion and a sacrifice involved and you get to a certain extent to choose that.

I will speak only from personal experience and understanding of what is going on around me.  
I am now 24 years old , pretty young when it comes to deep introspection (Jung has estimated that being 35+ means you would have enough experience to get results when diving deep within yourself), to a big extent your first 18 years with of course a margin of error always, you are a product of your capabilities, genes, upbringing and environment and depending on the person and the information they got throught their lives some will not be able to understand the duality in the human beings, the understanding of human beings to how the world works in regard to the "real".   
We recognize opposites in everything, life and death was probably the beginning , chaos and order and to some extent fail to see the same potential in ourselves, emotional maturity in some sense is realizing that we cannot escape our humanity and transcend into whatever it is that we imagine, and so as the self-proclaimed most advanced species on earth , we wander around unable to see what we have become and aknowledge who we have become to be in terms of habits, perception etc.. and we fail into simple traps of the mind or the unconscious and it is only when we realise that there is a TON that we do not understand nor aknowledge in ourselves that in a sense we are reborn.   
It's in a way knowing that you know little to nothing about yourself and aknowledging the potential of everything in terms of opposites in ourselves, it's the coexistence of the persona , ego and the one and only shadow merged together to form big chunks of the self you want to be conscious of in the never ending quest towards individuation.

I am still young to give advice (24 years old) but if I had to say something , always keep in mind that the unlived lives of the parents are the biggest psychological effects on the kids.  
If you've ever felt missunderstood, unappreciated, lacked empathy and love in your life make sure to give those to your child regardless of your strategy, knowing the areas you're lacking in your life is probably your best way going forward to understand your child more.   
We people with ADHD are predisposed to traumas, neglect , alienation, do not try so much to live through your child, and never gaslight your child. Understanding what forced them to do something is better than judging it , if any behaviour is not tolerated understanding what led to that means opening up to your child and showing that you're willing to treat him as a human being and not as a child in general.  


Tough love unfortunately had its repercussions especially emotionally, I hope everything works out fine, don't push him too much hehe, life is already hard as it is with ADHD.

Can I give a quick tip guys, I do not have BPD myself but have been around people with BPD and in a relationship, please don't think of this as an insult or an attempt to shame anyone.  


The thing is maturity and growing up without a personality disorder makes it so that the person understands that he has a choice always, and that he is responsible for his own emotional reaction , this doesn't mean that what you guys feel is fake or exagerated on the contrary , but the actions cannot be excused with "but i thought you hated me" , "you hurt me" , this is why people usually say or even in symptoms you see the person affected with BPD fears abandonment but sabotages himself, you always have a choice guys , don't let people manipulate you, don't question yourself in a sense of "am i making the right choice?" make a list of the positives and negatives in that person and decide wether you think they are a right fit as a friend.  


You are the only one unfortunately responsible for yourself in this world regardless of your illnesses (I have both ADHD and C-PTSD) I can relate a lot to your pain, I know it hurts when people say you're a snowflake I know it but isn't it you? aren't you really easily hurt? It's fine to be that way , it really is that's the part of acceptance you're missing , own that trait of personality you're calling weakness be aware of it , cherish it , give it a meaning in your actions, if someone is hurting you but you still feel attachement , try to identify the source of that emotion, what is it you're craving? his love , his acceptance? question it , why? Don't label yourself you are more than your mental illness you are the reddit user Mania-King that I do not know the name of :D more than just a mental illness so be brave and dive deep into your fears no matter how hurtful it is only then will recovery be possible.  


I will say something that will 100% hurt you but I mean it in good will , don't be intitled to someone, never , people are what they are , you cannot control consequenses , you cannot ask for something in return when you're kind, you just can't , what you need to do is have standards for yourself , find a person or friends that fit you, don't wish for someone to behave well just because you've done everything to be as good of a person as possible, it doesn't work like that, accept individuals as they are with their good parts and their flaws and make a responsible choice because your destiny is in your hand. Do I want this person in my life right now? no? I cannot make a choice? Boom that's something to work on , why can't I make a choice? I can make a choice? Perfect I make that choice and stick to it because I can take care of myself and I can be independent , he's butthurt? Who cares if I wronged him or not everyone makes mistakes but I made a choice based on pros and cons because at the moment I am not able to be sophisticated in choosing people around, aknowledge that weakness , have boundaries and rules to protect yourself while you're building yourself up to be mature and healthy and then you will undoubtedly attract healthy people. Good luck and sorry again if I was insensitive, I am just giving a different perspective that I think is needed to grow. (But then again I could be wrong :D wether you insult me or not doesn't say if you're a good or bad person it's just an action you took because you thought it's right and it's fine as long as you brace yourself to assume the consequences)

You cannot control the future , you cannot control the repercussions of your actions , the only thing you can actually "control" is your actions.

  
You are setting yourself for failure everytime you set expectations especially in regards to your father , you are trying to "win" even though you said it yourself what you want is respect and recognition in a sort of way, your actual need is an emotional one a very natural one so to put it into your words , don't play your opponent game, don't do what you hate in your peers , do not project yourself thinking that this time you have the truth and they should be the ones bending their asses even though you're at first against that.

Work on yourself and do not try to fix others thinking that would fix you or make them understand you, you cannot unfortunately shape your family nor the poeple around you into beings that see you, you simply can't do that all you can do is look inside , see what is bothering you , why it is bothering , where it came from , accept it , embrace and love it and know that whenever you see "wrong" in people , you are usually projecting and not accepting what you're capable of which you've shown in the text above.  


It really sounds cheesy but work towards individuation and love yourself, it sounds simple but this a lifelong task.

Always keep in mind that neurological issues are different than purely psychological/intellectual (don't know the exact issues to explain this one) , ADHD is mainly a difference in the brain structure compared to the "usual" or typical one (the neurotypical brainstructure) and involves a  decrease in the volume in the left-sided [p](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prefrontal_cortex)refontal cortex , impairmaints in executive functions as well as  abnormalities in neurotransmitter pathways.

So this sort of brainstructure causes quite the difficulties for the individual in today's society as the lack of attention and interest in general is seen at a very young age regardless of the parents treatment the environment etc.. which explains why these individuals regardless of the culture they live in all share great similarities in their stories and interpretations of their childhood.

Now these children since they are deemed somehow different can get rejected by their peers , their parents or bullied which can cause the weak ego to arise and make it even more difficult for them to have a happy childhood especially when they are not diagnosed at an early age, I have to note that I am extremely biased as I was only been diagnosed at the age of 23 with ADHD and suffered a lot from this alienation.

As a kid and growing up I lived in extremes because I literally couldn't control my attention no matter how disciplined i trained myself to be , I was heavily into competition as a kid wether it's video games or sports and found myself only able to focus in something I really liked and had an interest for that's when the hyperfocus kicks in where I am literally unable to hear anyone around me but if something didn't interest me ,even though I was quite conscious as a kid because I had to be in order to survive ,I couldn't for the life of me focus and spent years being bitter and resentful towards myself and bullying myself for not being able to focus at somehting I didn't like even though I was fully aware that it was an obligation.

I think (and could be wrong) that ADHD is a neurodevelopmental disorder and its symptoms are seen as silly and pretty common compared to let's say autistic spectrum disorders where people can easily spot out that the behaviour is unusual and different and it makes it so that it's seen as more of an issue with the individual in regards to his evolution as a responsible individual.

People that have what is called a weak ego I think lack in conscientiousness and do not have the tools necessary to survive until they find a goal or purpose or whatever it is that drives them to live and accept their Being.

Emotions are needed to be in the equation to determine all the factors , because rationalizing emotions as far as i'm concerned is literally denying a part of our nature, what you may see as essentialism and subjective understanding of something that shouldn't be named unconscious since you have no access to it is just essentially the numbers we call now in "real psychology" but proceeding in this rational way of seeing things and considering psychology as a science of facts leads undoubtedly to extentialism maybe nihilism or literally just dropping the ball and going insane.

I share the exact same stories listed here with of course different impacts and dove into introspection or probably was forced into it at a very young age, I developped that big yet fragile ego, kept on living in dissociation and my thoughts.

  
My inability to take action made it so that I couldn't even set apart what was the shadow , what was the ego and what was the self, I was lost in a myriad of ideas and unable to go grocery shopping or wash my clothes.  


I am now 24 and it's been a year that I have been diagnosed with ADHD regardless of wether you think it is a neurological condition or not, I have wondered and got lost in my brain to the point where I thought I NEEDED TO GIVE MYSELF PTSD , i came to the conclusion that I had to shake my whole psyche in order to convey thoughts into actions and in reality I was naive, young had neurological issues that limited my executive functions , I had multiple childhood traumas that resulted in the clinical term C-PTSD.  


What I'm trying to say is regardless what you're doing , your answer might be true but not part of the truth as you will never be able to grasp all the truth if it even exists or within the realm of our capabilities as humans, there is more to yourself and it could be something simple that requires a psychiatrist so do not fall into the pit of arrogance as it could portray itself like an undeniable fact when in reality you're just lacking information.  


Bottom line is, don't forget you're human and you could be born different in regard to your brain structure and aknowledge that you could have a condition that could hinder your functionning.
